column3: The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”
The Hebrew repeats “the altar” in the final clause and calls it “holiness of holinesses”; BSB uses “it” and “most holy.”
The Hebrew ends “consecrate it,” with a singular object; BSB says “consecrate them.”
The Hebrew repeats the action, ending “so he did”; BSB expresses Moses’ obedience once.
The Hebrew ends “as the LORD commanded Moses”; BSB replaces the repeated name with “him.”
The Hebrew uses an unnamed “he” and says he put the poles “on the ark”; BSB names Moses and describes the poles as being attached to it.
The Hebrew ends “as the LORD commanded Moses”; BSB replaces the repeated name with “him.”
The Hebrew has an unnamed “he” and uses the body image “thigh” for the tabernacle’s side; BSB names Moses and says “side.”
The Hebrew says he “arranged an arrangement of bread” and ends with Moses’ name; BSB reduces the repeated arrangement wording and uses “him.”
The Hebrew uses the body image “thigh” for the tabernacle’s side; BSB says “side” and adds “also.”
The Hebrew ends “as the LORD commanded Moses”; BSB replaces the repeated name with “him.”
The Hebrew says “he placed”; BSB supplies the name Moses.
The Hebrew ends “as the LORD commanded Moses”; BSB replaces the repeated name with “him.”
The Hebrew places the altar “at the entrance” and ends with Moses’ name; BSB says “near the entrance” and replaces the name with “him.”
